function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

message.content: Below is a practical, step‑by‑step playbook you can follow to turn your e‑commerce idea into a polished, production‑ready front‑end. I’ll cover the whole stack—from choosing a framework to deploying and monitoring—so you can pick the parts that fit your team’s skill set and your product vision. --- ## 1️⃣ Define the Scope & Gather Requirements | What | Why it matters | |------|----------------| | **Target audience** | Mobile‑first vs desktop‑heavy influences layout, touch targets, and performance goals. | | **Core features** | Product catalog, search, filters, cart, checkout flow, user account, reviews, wish‑lists, admin panel. | | **Performance goals** | First Contentful Paint < 2 s, Time to Interactive < 5 s, Lighthouse score > 90. | | **Accessibility** | WCAG 2.1 AA compliance ensures broader reach and better SEO. | | **Analytics & tracking** | Google Analytics, Mixpanel, or custom event bus for conversion funnels. | > **Tip:** Create a *feature backlog* in Jira/Trello and prioritize by business value + effort. --- ## 2️⃣ Choose Your Front‑End Stack | Option | Pros | Cons | When to Pick It | |--------|------|------|-----------------| | **React + Vite / CRA** | Huge ecosystem, reusable components, great tooling, SSR via Next.js | Learning curve if you’re new to JSX | Most modern projects; strong community support | | **Vue 3 + Vite** | Simpler learning curve, Composition API, excellent dev experience | Smaller ecosystem than React | Teams comfortable with Vue or looking for a lighter bundle | | **Angular** | Opinionated, built‑in DI, RxJS, CLI scaffolding | Verbose, heavier bundle | Enterprise teams needing strict architecture | | **SvelteKit** | Zero runtime overhead, compile‑time optimizations | Smaller ecosystem, less mature | Projects where bundle size is critical | ### Recommendation If you’re starting fresh, **React + Vite** (or **Next.js** for SSR) gives you the most flexibility and a huge pool of ready‑made components. If you already have a Vue background, go with Vue 3 + Vite. --- ## 3️⃣ Project Skeleton & Tooling ```bash # Example with Vite + React npm create vite@latest ecommerce-frontend --template react cd ecommerce-frontend npm install ``` | Tool | Purpose | Suggested Packages | |------|---------|--------------------| | **TypeScript** | Static typing, IDE autocomplete | `typescript`, `@types/react` | | **ESLint + Prettier** | Code quality & formatting | `eslint`, `prettier`, `eslint-config-prettier` | | **Storybook** | Component library sandbox | `@storybook/react` | | **Jest + Testing Library** | Unit & integration tests | `jest`, `@testing-library/react` | | **Vite** | Fast dev server & HMR | Built‑in | | **Tailwind CSS** | Utility‑first styling | `tailwindcss`, `postcss`, `autoprefixer` | | **React Query / SWR** | Data fetching & caching | `react-query` or `swr` | | **Redux Toolkit / Zustand** | Global state (if needed) | `@reduxjs/toolkit`, `zustand` | | **React Router** | Client‑side routing | `react-router-dom` | | **i18next** | Internationalisation | `react-i18next` | | **CI/CD** | GitHub Actions or GitLab CI | `.github/workflows/*` | > **Pro Tip:** Keep your dependencies minimal at first; add only what you need as the project grows. --- ## 4️⃣ Design System & UI Components | Step | Action | |------|--------| | **Wireframe** | Sketch or Figma → low‑fidelity mockups of key pages (home, product list, product detail, cart, checkout). | | **Prototype** | Add interactions in Figma → click‑through prototype for stakeholder review. | | **Design Tokens** | Extract colors, spacing, typography into JSON or SCSS variables. | | **Component Library** | Build reusable components: ` > ); > ``` --- ## 5️⃣ State Management & Data Layer | Concern | Solution | |---------|----------| | **Fetching product data** | `react-query` handles caching, refetching, optimistic updates. | | **Cart & Wishlist** | Local state (React Context) or global store (Redux Toolkit). Persist to `localStorage` or IndexedDB for offline support. | | **User authentication** | JWT stored in HttpOnly cookies; use `react-query` to fetch user profile. | | **Search & Filters** | Debounced input with `lodash.debounce`; query parameters sync with URL for shareable links. | | **SSR / ISR** | Next.js pages pre-rendered at build time or on demand. | > **Code Snippet – Cart Context** > ```ts > // cartContext.tsx > import { createContext, useReducer, useContext } from 'react'; > > type CartItem = { id: string; quantity: number }; > type CartState = { items: CartItem[] }; > type CartAction = > | { type: 'ADD'; item: CartItem } > | { type: 'REMOVE'; id: string } > | { type: 'CLEAR' }; > > const reducer = (state: CartState, action: CartAction): CartState => { > switch (action.type) { > case 'ADD': > return { items: [...state.items, action.item] }; > case 'REMOVE': > return { items: state.items.filter(i => i.id !== action.id) }; > case 'CLEAR': > return { items: [] }; > default: > return state; > } > }; > > const CartContext = createContext<{ > state: CartState; > dispatch: React.Dispatch; > }>({ state: { items: [] }, dispatch: () => null }); > > export const CartProvider = ({ children }) => { > const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, { items: [] }); > return {children}; > }; > > export const useCart = () => useContext(CartContext); > ``` --- ## 6️⃣ Routing & Navigation | Feature | Implementation | |---------|----------------| | **Dynamic routes** | `/products/[slug].tsx` in Next.js or `Route path="/product/:id"` in React Router. | | **Nested layouts** | Layout components for header/footer, sidebar, etc. | | **Protected routes** | Higher‑order component that checks auth status before rendering. | | **SEO meta tags** | `next/head` or `react-helmet` to inject title, description, OpenGraph tags. | --- ## 7️⃣ API Integration | API Type | Recommended Library | |----------|---------------------| | **REST** | Axios or Fetch API wrapped in `react-query` hooks. | | **GraphQL** | Apollo Client or urql. | | **Serverless Functions** | Deploy API endpoints as Netlify Functions or Vercel Serverless. | | **Payment Gateway** | Stripe Elements or Braintree SDK. | > **Example – Fetch products with React Query** > ```ts > // hooks/useProducts.ts > import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'; > import axios from 'axios'; > > export const useProducts = (page = 1) => > useQuery(['products', page], async () => { > const { data } = await axios.get(`/api/products?page=${page}`); > return data; > }); > ``` --- ## 8️⃣ Performance Optimisation | Technique | How | |-----------|-----| | **Code splitting** | Dynamic imports (`import()`) for heavy modules. | | **Image optimisation** | Use ``, next/image in Next.js, or Cloudinary transformations. | | **Critical CSS** | Inline small CSS chunks for above‑the‑fold content. | | **Bundle analysis** | `webpack-bundle-analyzer` or Vite’s built‑in visualiser. | | **Service Workers** | Cache assets and API responses for offline shopping. | | **Prefetching** | `react-query`’s `prefetchQuery` for anticipated navigation. | --- ## 9️⃣ Accessibility Checklist | Check | Tool | |-------|------| | **Keyboard navigation** | Tab order, focus ring visible. | | **ARIA labels** | `aria-label`, `role="button"`, `aria-live` for dynamic content. | | **Contrast ratio** | WCAG 2.1 AA (≥ 4.5:1 for normal text). | | **Screen reader test** | NVDA/VoiceOver + axe-core. | | **Alt text** | Descriptive image alt attributes. | > **Automated audit**: Run `npx axe-core` or integrate `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`. --- ## 🔟 Testing Strategy | Test Level | Tool | Focus | |------------|------|-------| | **Unit** | Jest + React Testing Library | Individual components, hooks. | | **Integration** | Cypress | End‑to‑end flows (add to cart, checkout). | | **Visual regression** | Percy or Chromatic | Detect unintended UI changes. | | **Load testing** | k6 or Locust | Backend API resilience under traffic spikes. | --- ## 1️⃣1️⃣ Deployment & DevOps | Platform | Notes | |----------|-------| | **Vercel** | Great for Next.js, automatic SSR, preview URLs. | | **Netlify** | Good for static sites, edge functions. | | **AWS Amplify** | Full‑stack hosting, easy CI/CD pipelines. | | **Docker + Kubernetes** | For micro‑services or custom infra. | ### CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions example) ```yaml name: CI on: push: branches: [ main ] pull_request: jobs: build-test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: actions/setup-node@v3 with: node-version: '20' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm run test -- --coverage - run: npm run build - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3 with: name: build path: dist/ ``` Deploy to Vercel automatically after successful build: ```yaml deploy: needs: build-test runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/download-artifact@v3 with: name: build - uses: amondnet/vercel-action@v20 with: vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }} vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }} vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }} alias-domains: staging.example.com ``` --- ## 1️⃣2️⃣ Monitoring & Analytics | Tool | Purpose | |------|---------| | **Google Analytics 4** | Pageviews, events, funnel analysis. | | **Mixpanel** | User journey tracking, cohort analysis. | | **LogRocket** | Session replay, error capture. | | **Sentry** | Runtime error monitoring. | | **New Relic** | Application performance monitoring (APM). | > **Implementation tip:** Wrap your app in a global error boundary that reports to Sentry and logs to console for debugging. --- ## 1️⃣3️⃣ Security Best Practices | Area | Recommendation | |------|----------------| | **HTTPS** | Enforce TLS everywhere; use Cloudflare or AWS ACM. | | **CSP** | Content Security Policy to mitigate XSS. | | **XSS protection** | Escape all user‑generated content; use DOMPurify for rich text. | | **CSRF tokens** | For forms that modify state; use SameSite cookies. | | **Rate limiting** | Protect checkout endpoint against bots. | | **Dependency scanning** | Dependabot or Renovate for automated vulnerability alerts. | --- ## 1️⃣4️⃣ Final Checklist Before Launch | Item | Done? | |------|-------| | ✅ Responsive design tested on mobile, tablet, desktop | | ✅ Accessibility audit passed (WCAG 2.1 AA) | | ✅ All core flows unit‑tested (≥ 80% coverage) | | ✅ E2E tests passing (Cypress) | | ✅ Performance metrics meet target (Lighthouse ≥ 90) | | ✅ Error handling & logging configured | | ✅ CI/CD pipeline fully automated | | ✅ Deployment to production environment | | ✅ Backup strategy for database & media | | ✅ GDPR / privacy policy & cookie banner implemented | --- ## 🎉 Next Steps 1. **Kick off the design sprint** – create high‑fidelity prototypes in Figma. 2. **Set up the repo** – scaffold with Vite + React, add ESLint, Prettier, Storybook. 3. **Build the component library** – start with Buttons, Cards, Modals. 4. **Integrate the API layer** – write hooks with `react-query`. 5. **Add authentication** – JWT + Auth0 or Firebase Auth. 6. **Write tests** – unit + Cypress. 7. **Deploy to Vercel** – preview URLs for stakeholders. 8. **Run performance & accessibility audits** – iterate until thresholds met. 9. **Launch** – monitor with Sentry, LogRocket, GA4. Feel free to ask for deeper dives into any of the sections—whether you need a starter template, a specific hook implementation, or help configuring CI/CD. Happy coding!
